title: Colgan Air Flight 3407: stall-warning response, monitoring, sterile cockpit, fatigue, and oversight surfaces
summary: Colgan 3407 is encoded as a flight-deck monitoring and stall-response case with supervision, professionalism, fatigue, training, records, and FAA oversight kept visible as separate factors.

status_history.note: Added as rev0027 flight-deck state / CRM rail lane record.

place.location: Clarence Center, New York, United States

claims.claim: The NTSB page identifies Colgan Air Flight 3407 as a February 12, 2009 DHC-8-400 crash into a residence near Clarence Center, New York, with 49 people aboard and one person on the ground killed.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The NTSB probable-cause/contributing-factors summary identifies the captain’s inappropriate response to stick-shaker activation leading to aerodynamic stall, and lists contributing factors including flightcrew monitoring failures, sterile cockpit nonadherence, captain management, and Colgan procedures.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The NTSB safety-issues list for Colgan 3407 includes monitoring failures, professionalism, fatigue, remedial training, pilot training records, stall training, FAA oversight, FOQA, portable electronic devices, and safety alerts, with related FAA recommendations issued.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

Do not flatten human-factors findings into pilot blame; separate physical system state, displayed state, automation mode, training, procedures, supervision, fatigue, and investigation/legal status.
This is historical/evidentiary infrastructure, not operational flight-safety guidance or legal advice.
